query: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets provide 16 candidate alloys, nine of which are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing. Early reports associated increasing constituent count with greater strength, but that simple relationship is no longer generally accepted. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical investigation, the origins of differences in deformation and failure behavior remain unresolved; practical interpretation must also account for constituent cost and overall cost-performance balance. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs these mechanical-property differences and why? Define a controlled investigation, the observations predicted relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the limits within which the hypothesis should apply, the prior evidence supporting it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The differences in mechanical properties among the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloys and their subsets are governed by the variation in the local lattice distortion caused by the differences in atomic radii of the constituent elements.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets in single-phase FCC structure after thermomechanical processing
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of the constituent elements to alter the local lattice distortion
generation.mechanism: The variation in local lattice distortion affects the dislocation mobility and the resulting deformation behavior, leading to differences in mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloys with higher local lattice distortion will exhibit higher strength and lower ductility compared to the equiatomic quinary baseline
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to single-phase FCC alloys with constituent elements having significant differences in atomic radii
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between local lattice distortion and mechanical properties is not well established, and the role of other factors such as grain size and texture is not considered

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of the constituent elements to alter the local lattice distortion, followed by uniaxial tensile testing
measurements: Lattice distortion, dislocation density, mechanical properties (strength, ductility)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the observed relationship between local lattice distortion and mechanical properties does not follow the predicted trend, the hypothesis is falsified
